title: Functional Difference-in-Differences Curve Estimation with Measurement Error and Arbitrary Visit Counts
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded tier=subfield below field floor: paper_score_ceiling 7.0 < 7.4; calibrated class has narrow reach and no delivered application or computation.
gap_reasons: The substantive limitation is the calibrated experiment: exactly uniform control covariates, balanced recruitment, known randomized visit densities, and ten-dimensional Lipschitz confounding do not establish a frontier for general observational functional DiD.
The prospective NCANDA-A and ULEZ references supply no application result, and no delivered computation establishes the estimator's finite-sample usefulness near the proposed crossover.
The TL;DR's unqualified minimax-risk formula overstates this as an exact risk characterization.
Both converse constructions reuse Pi_0 and Q_0 for the null and the location-zero alternative, requiring a notation repair to make their statements unambiguous.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 closed the matched all-finite-visit frontier for the calibrated class and D0.5 math and decision panels passed, including attested Fano and Bernstein citations. F2 emitted a compiling 73-node Lean scaffold, but formalization did not reach F5 because the field novelty floor failed after the source was repaired. A future field-tier run would need a broader observational target or delivered operational evidence; the TL;DR qualification and null/alternative notation also need cleanup.
tldr: For fixed nondegenerate radii \(L_a,M_b,L_b,M_\tau,L_\tau,V>0\) and positive measurement-error variance budget \(\sigma_\varepsilon^2>0\), the calibrated two-period functional DiD experiment with exactly \(n\) independent people and any finite integer \(m\ge1\) randomized noisy visits per period has expected-supremum minimax risk \(r_{n,m}=\max\{[\log(en)/(n^2m)]^{2/15},[\log(en)/n^2]^{1/7}\}\). The observable coarse-median/fine-cell-clipping estimator, using one positive class/design envelope witness fixed before sampling and shared by every fine threshold, attains this rate, and exact fixed-\(n\) Gaussian sparse-visit and bounded Bernoulli full-curve mixtures give the same-class converse. The positive budget is only an upper bound, so individual class members may have zero measurement noise. The bounded Bernoulli dense floor remains valid even when the budget itself is zero. The channels meet at \(m_\star=n^{1/7}\{\log(en)\}^{-1/14}\); on the positive-budget domain, visits improve the order below this crossover and the full-curve confounding floor governs above it.
gap: Functional DiD inference currently relies on person-level reconstruction that is negligible at the root-\(n\) scale. The banked sparse-visit analysis leaves an extra upper-bound logarithm, states a sparse logarithmic converse without the independently auditable construction required here, and has only a one-location scalar dense floor. The exact one-logarithm upper envelope and the full-curve dense-visit floor remain unresolved.
fill: The hybrid estimator uses ordinary block medians only where spatial cell means are too large and uses clipping only where independent parent cells have small total squared means. The sparse converse uses a raw-visit Gaussian sign mixture over disjoint temporal windows, and the dense converse uses a separate bounded Bernoulli oracle sign mixture. Together these constructions target a same-class matched fixed-\(n\) theorem and an attained subject-versus-visit crossover.
